title: Hospitality handler & graceful shedding for hosted API 5xx/timeouts during escalations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:

This ticket scopes and drives implementation of a lightweight "hospitality handler" plus graceful shedding primitives in the Hosted API to reduce customer-visible 5xx/timeouts and retry-amplification during tenant surges and customer escalations. The hospitality handler is a runtime and edge coordination pattern that attempts to maintain a useful customer experience (cached or abbreviated responses, fallback variants, informative headers) before resorting to hard failures that trigger client retries and cascade failure modes.

Background and motivation:
Recent escalations show repeated cycles where backend kernel slowdowns or KV cache evictions cause latency > SLO, customers' SDKs retry aggressively, and proxy fanout multiplies load leading to 5xx waves. Existing mitigations (circuit breakers, tenant shaping) are effective but blunt: they fail fast with generic errors which frequently prompt customers to retry or open escalations. A hospitality-first approach aims to reduce the incidence and severity of escalations by performing graded degradation that preserves functionality and provides better signals to SDKs and the Console.

Goals:
- Reduce customer-visible 5xx and timeout rates by 40% during tenant surges.
- Lower retry amplification by providing explicit, machine-readable degrade signals so SDKs can backoff more intelligently.
- Maintain correctness: never return misleading hallucinated content; degraded outputs must be safe-labeled.
- Provide easy kill-switches for on-call and a per-tenant opt-out for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Key design components (high level):
1) Detection & classifier: runtime rule that marks requests as "hospitality-eligible" when latency or kernel queue depth crosses thresholds, or when tenant has >X inflight requests.
2) Hospitality handler chain (ordered):
   a) Serve prefix or cached completions from KV cache with a header x-rd-hospitality: cached; mark as partial=true.
   b) Attempt a degraded fast-path using a small-context lightweight model variant (compatible tokenizer) returning summarized output + provenance header.
   c) If neither is possible, return an informative 429-like degrade object with guidance and backoff headers (x-rd-suggested-backoff, x-rd-can-retry-after) rather than a generic 500.
3) Backpressure signaling: inject headers consumed by SDKs and Console to reduce client retry aggressiveness.
4) Per-tenant concurrency semaphore and prioritized queues that let hospitality keep a small number of fast-path slots for premium tenants.
5) Observability: new Grafana panels, SLO burn metrics, and an incident-dedicated trace sampling rate.

Implementation tasks (rough):
- Runtime: request classifier + hospitality handler dispatch point in request lifecycle (ENG runtime team)
- Edge proxy: add header plumbing and fast-routing behavior for hospitality responses (proxy team)
- SDK: implement backoff/ header handling + guidance in docs (DX/SDK)
- Console: add table view for hospitality events by tenant + explainability UI (Console team)
- Runbook: on-call steps to disable hospitality or adjust thresholds per region/cluster

Rollout plan:
- Canary 10% of tenants (internal customers and a subset of non-critical customers) for 48h.
- Ramp to 50% for 24h, monitor SLOs and retry amplification metrics.
- Full rollout 72h after green signal; keep enhanced tracing for 7d.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for classifier and handler decision tree.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with KV cache and lightweight model variant fallback.
- Chaostorm tests: simulate kernel slowdowns and KV evictions to validate degrade behavior.
- Customer canary: coordinate with two willing customers for production canary and feedback.

Customer communication and escalation playbook:
- Draft template for proactive customer outreach when hospitality is enabled for their tenant (include links to Console hospitality logs).
- On-call playbook: how to flip per-tenant hospitality, how to read hospitality headers, and how to temporarily increase quotas if needed.

Dedicated/Private considerations:
- Expose toggle via config and operator API.
- Make default off for Private until validated by customers with on-premops.

Success metrics:
- 40% drop in customer-visible 5xx and timeouts within surge windows.
- 50% reduction in median retries per failed request during incidents.
- Positive customer feedback in canary cohort.

Notes & non-goals:
- This is not a substitute for fixing root causes (kernel bugs, connection pool leaks). Those fixes remain tracked separately. Hospitality is a tactical mitigation to reduce blast radius and improve customer experience during incidents.
